title: They were dying of thirst…
paragraphs:
They were dying of thirst…
and the water in front of them made it worse.
Bitter.
Undrinkable.
Poison to the soul.
In Exodus 15, Israel stood at Marah—three days in the wilderness, lips cracked, hope fading. They found water…
…but it only deepened their desperation.
And they complained.
Loud.
Raw.
Human.

Then God gave an instruction that didn’t make sense:
Throw a piece of wood into the water.

Not filter it.
Not boil it.
Not analyze it.
Obey.

Moses obeyed…
and the bitter water became sweet.
Pause.
Because this isn’t just about water.
This is about you.

That relationship that turned toxic.
That season that tastes like disappointment.
That prayer that feels unanswered.
Bitter.
And here’s what we miss…
God often places the “wood” near our pain before He changes the condition of our pain.
Obedience comes before transformation.

The wood in Marah whispers of another tree—
the cross of Jesus Christ.

Because at the cross, the bitterness of sin was swallowed by grace.
What should have destroyed us… became the very place we were healed.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
Your life may taste bitter right now.

But when you surrender—
when you obey even when it doesn’t make sense—
God steps in and rewrites the outcome.

From poison… to provision.
From pain… to purpose.
From bitter… to sweet.

Jesus doesn’t just change circumstances.
He changes the condition of the heart.
So don’t run from the bitter place.
Listen.
There might be a cross waiting there.
And that’s where grace walks in.
